reason: This text recounts the story of Cain and Abel (Genesis 4:1-16), depicting their occupations as a shepherd and tiller of the ground, respectively. Rather than demonstrating collaboration and working together, the narrative shows competition and conflict: Cain becomes jealous when God favors Abel's offering over his own, his anger escalates, and ultimately he kills his brother in the field. The passage emphasizes their separate endeavors, God's differential treatment of their offerings, and culminates in fratricide rather than any form of collaborative effort between the characters.
